subject: dUnif and dcat - JAGs to nimble

messages.author: c30f454051765351
messages.subject: dUnif and dcat - JAGs to nimble
parts:
Hi Everyone, 
I apologize if this is answered elsewhere, I searched through the google group archives and on the web and r-nimble website but couldn't find the answer to my issue. 

I am working on joint likelihood integrated population models, in this current case with a multi-state capture recapture submodel. In JAGs the code to define the priors for population at first time step is: 
 N[1,1] ~ dcat(pinit) # 1st age class
 N[2,1] ~ dcat(pinit) # 2nd age class

where `pinit` is defined in the jags data object as: 
pinit <- dUnif(1,300)

dUnif is a jags function that is meant to be used with dcat to generate discrete uniform priors. When I try to use this with nimble I get the following error:

Defining model
  [Note] Using 'C,marr.a,marr.j,sJ1,sJ2' (given within 'constants') as data.
Warning in replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :
  Code pinit was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar.  This is probably not what you want.
Warning in replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :
  Code pinit was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar.  This is probably not what you want.
Error in replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :
  Error, hit end

Thanks in advance to everyone!

messages.author: c30f454051765351
messages.subject: Re: dUnif and dcat - JAGs to nimble
parts:
Hi All, 
Just want to update that I got some good help and figured it out. I just had to specify indexing on pinit within the dcat() function as: dcat( pinit[1:300] )

Thanks!

Ok, glad you figured it out.  

Just a note that I wasn't quite understanding your comment about a discrete uniform prior for 'pinit', since 'pinit' needs to be a vector of probabilities that add to 1. 

-Chris

messages.subject: Re: dUnif and dcat - JAGs to nimble
parts:
Thank you Chris,

 

Sorry I was somewhat unclear describing the problem. The jags function dUnif() is essentially a shortcut to create a probability vector that passes to dcat() to generate the multinomial priors. The issue I had was simply that I didn’t specify the indexing on the pinit vector within dcat.

Thanks!

Ben
